overview: White fianchettoes against the Dutch, the most popular way to meet it. After 3...e6 4.Bg2 Black chooses between ...d5 (Stonewall/Classical set-ups) and ...Be7 with ...O-O and ...d6 (Classical). White controls e4 and aims for a central break, e4 or d5, while Black plays for kingside space and control of e4. The positions are strategic but unbalanced, with Black's weakened e8-h5 diagonal and e4 square the key issues.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the king's bishop and control e4 and the long diagonal
Break with d5 or e4 depending on Black's set-up
Exploit the weakened e8-h5 diagonal and the e6-pawn

black_ideas.idea: Control e4 and build kingside space with ...d5 or ...d6 and ...Ne4
Attack on the kingside with ...Qe8-h5 and ...g5-type pawn pushes
Stay compact in a Stonewall or Classical structure

character.notes: Dutch positions are unbalanced; both sides seek active kingside or central play.

structure.notes: Main line 3...e6 4.Nf3 d5 (Stonewall) locks the centre; Classical lines keep tension.

approach.notes: Standard Dutch defence, used by strong players such as Nakamura and Carlsen.

level.notes: Structures are subtle with e4/f5 imbalances; plans take understanding.
